passages.text: HEART, in anatomy, a hollow muscular body, situated in the breast between the two lobes of the lungs, which by its contraction drives the blood through the arteries.
It has two ventricles, or cavities, separated by a partition, and two auricles; the right ventricle sends the blood to the lungs, and the left through the whole body.
The circulation of the blood through the heart, arteries, and veins was discovered by our countryman Dr William Harvey, who published it in 1628.
The valves at the mouths of the vessels permit the blood to pass one way only, and hinder its return.
In a grown man the heart contracts about seventy-five times in a minute.
The motion of the heart is thought to be caused by the nervous influence flowing to it from the brain.
The ancients made the heart the seat of the passions and of courage; and the expressions of common speech still bear the marks of that opinion.
The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood through the blood vessels. In humans it lies in the chest between the lungs, slightly to the left.
The human heart has four chambers: two upper atria and two lower ventricles. The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs and the left ventricle pumps it to the rest of the body.
William Harvey described the circulation of the blood in his book De Motu Cordis, published in 1628.
Heart valves keep blood flowing in one direction through the heart.
The resting heart rate of an adult is typically 60 to 100 beats per minute.
The heartbeat starts in the heart itself, in a group of pacemaker cells called the sinoatrial node. Nerves can speed it up or slow it down but do not start each beat.
The heart was long believed to be the seat of emotion and thought. It remains a common symbol of love.

What did the 1797 entry think makes the.answer: A nervous influence flowing to it from the brain [B6]. Wikipedia says the beat starts in the heart itself, in the pacemaker cells of the sinoatrial node; nerves can speed it up or slow it down but do not start each beat [W6].

How much of the 1797 description of the.answer: Most of it. The four chambers [B2] [W2], Harvey's circulation of 1628 [B3] [W3], one-way valves [B4] [W4] and a rate of about 75 beats a minute [B5] [W5] all hold. The claim that the brain drives the beat [B6] does not [W6].
